newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine attacks his "Dirty War" tormentor Astiz.
newsitem.headline: Argentine attacks his "Dirty War" tormentor Astiz.

text.p: An Argentine whose family were victims of the military's "Dirty War" in the late 1970s attacked Thursday the man who tortured his wife and child -- former Navy captain Alfredo Astiz, dubbed the "Blond Angel."
"Why don't you torture me now?" Jorge Ocampo shouted at Astiz before trying in vain to land a punch, in the second incident this week involving Astiz.

Astiz has become a hated symbol of the 1976-83 military dictatorship's campaign against suspected leftists in which thousands of Argentines were killed. France and Sweden want to jail him for the murders of citizens of both countries.
Ocampo, who was forced into exile in Sweden in 1976 after his family was interrogated and beaten, told local radio how he had recognised Astiz outside a cafe in Buenos Aires.

"When I saw who it was, despite the fact that he was covering his face, I hit out at him but didn't manage to punch him," said Ocampo, who was sought by the military because of his membership of the Peronist Party, which is now in power.
"This morning all those memories came back -- when he hit my wife and threw my daughter on the floor and grabbed her by the hair," said Ocampo.

Astiz was tried and jailed for his human rights crimes, and for cowardice in the 1982 Falklands War with Britain, after democracy was restored in 1983. Like other Dirty War officers and guerrillas, he benefited from an amnesty in 1989.
His public appearances have repeatedly provoked attacks. In the Andean ski resort of Bariloche he was punched in the street and this weekend he was spat at in a nightclub.
